title: Implement Atomistic Simulation Framework
action: Implement the atomistic simulation for a bcc bicrystal. Load the Johnson pair potential and the Finnis-Sinclair N-body potential for alpha-iron. Construct the simulation cell (800 atomic rows in a 20a0x20a0 central region, (100) interface at x=0, lattice parameter a0=0.286 nm). Implement the elastic image construction for a screw dislocation in a bimaterial, conjugate-gradient energy minimization with an applied uniform shear strain, and the measurement of core half-width from the distribution of screw relative displacements across the {110} glide plane.
description: Sets up the complete simulation environment required for the subsequent computations.

title: Compute Homogeneous Reference Core Widths
action: For each interatomic potential, simulate a homogeneous crystal (no interface) containing a dislocation. Apply a small uniform shear strain to stabilise the dislocation at a Peierls valley equilibrium. After relaxation, compute the core half-width and configuration type. Record these values internally for later inclusion in the scored output files.
description: Establishes baseline core half-widths (~1.6 a0 for the pair potential, ~3 a0 for the N-body potential).

title: Compute Core Widths for Johnson Pair Potential
action: Using the Johnson pair potential, run bicrystal simulations at dislocation positions x = -2.5, -1.5, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 a0 from the interface. For each, apply the appropriate uniform shear strain to maintain equilibrium. After conjugate-gradient relaxation, measure the core half-width (in units of a0) and identify the configuration type. Include the homogeneous reference width as a row with position 'homogeneous'. Write a CSV file with columns position_a0, core_width_a0, configuration_type.
description: Scored core half-widths for the Johnson pair potential; verifies the asymmetry of core changes at the interface.
output_schema: Header: position_a0, core_width_a0, configuration_type. Rows for x = -2.5, -1.5, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and one row with position='homogeneous'. core_width_a0 is a positive float. configuration_type is a string such as '2C', '4C'.

title: Compute Core Widths for N-body Potential
action: Using the Finnis-Sinclair N-body potential, run bicrystal simulations at the same seven dislocation positions as in step 3. For each, apply the appropriate shear strain, relax, measure the core half-width and configuration type. Include the homogeneous reference width as a row. Write a CSV file with columns position_a0, core_width_a0, configuration_type.
description: Scored core half-widths for the N-body potential; validates the dramatic widening and dissociation in the hard medium.
output_schema: Same format as core_widths_pair_potential.csv. Rows for x = -2.5, -1.5, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and one row with position='homogeneous'.
